origin: aca-subsidies-left. Core claims are accurate (22.1 to 19.2 million paid enrollment, 58% higher premium payments, young adults a large share of the drop, insurers pricing in a sicker pool). Overstatement: "Every one of those 3 million people is now uninsured." The survey shows most 2025 enrollees who left the Marketplace moved to other coverage: 22% other coverage against 9% uninsured, so about 71% of leavers (22 of 31 points; computed by the case author). The "premiums will keep climbing" line is a forecast the fact sheet supports only through projections and 2026 filings. Expected honest rating: 55 to 70. aca-subsidies-right. Core claims are accurate (temporary credits originally due to end in 2022, sign-ups down about 5% to 23.1 million, 9% of 2025 enrollees uninsured, more leavers found other coverage than became uninsured). Overstatement: "Hardly anyone lost coverage", while paid enrollment fell by about 3 million (13%) and 9% of 2025 enrollees report being uninsured. The "premiums will settle down" line is a forecast that the fact sheet's risk-pool projections already lean against. Expected honest rating: 45 to 65.

evidence_up.evidence_note: Real. Peterson-KFF Health System Tracker, "How much and why ACA Marketplace premiums are going up in 2027", https://www.healthsystemtracker.org/brief/how-much-and-why-aca-marketplace-premiums-are-going-up-in-2027/. Published 2026-07-08, modified 2026-08-03 (page metadata). Verified: 276 insurers, 63% between 10% and 25%, 25th and 75th percentiles 11% and 22%, 51 insurers above 25%, one decrease, 2026 median proposed 18%, median 2027 medical trend 10% (among the 77 insurers reviewed in detail), "Individual market insurers are expecting the market to continue to deteriorate in 2027", healthier enrollees left leaving a sicker pool, about 4 percentage points for 2026 and again for 2027 among insurers adjusting for it. No 2027 filings brief appears before July 8 in the tracker's sitemap. KFF quick take, "ACA Marketplace Insurers Are Proposing a Median Premium Increase of About 15% in 2027", published 2026-08-04, https://www.kff.org/quick-insights/aca-marketplace-insurers-are-proposing-a-median-premium-increase-of-about-15-in-2027/. Verified: "the 15% median increase would be the second consecutive year of double-digit premium hikes (last year's median finalized premium increase was 20%.)"
pushes: New information that adds to the fact sheet: in July and August 2026, KFF's Peterson-KFF Health System Tracker published its review of the 2027 ACA Marketplace rate filings, which were available from all 50 states and the District of Columbia by early August. Among 276 insurers, most proposed 2027 premium increases between 10% and 25%, and 51 insurers asked for more than 25%; only one proposed a decrease. KFF put the median proposed increase at about 15%, which would be the second year in a row of double-digit increases after a median finalized increase of 20% for 2026. Rising medical costs (a median medical trend of 10% among insurers whose filings KFF reviewed in detail) are the main driver, but insurers also cite the expiration of the enhanced premium tax credits: KFF and insurers say healthier enrollees were more likely to drop coverage in 2026, leaving a somewhat sicker and more expensive pool, and insurers that adjusted for this project it will push 2027 premiums about 4 percentage points higher than they otherwise would be. Insurers expect the individual market to keep deteriorating in 2027. These are proposed rates and may change in review. Does that change your rating?
Makes sense. What is your final number?
